raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #8831

## Problem

For `elems_per_row <= 128` the inference v2 norm launchers pack several rows into one 256-thread block, but the kernels have no row bound. When `rows` is larger than the rows per block and not a multiple of it, the last, partially filled block loads and stores rows past the end of every input and output. Reachable through `CUDARMSNorm` with a small `channels`, e.g. the per-head Q/K RMSNorm of EXAONE4 / EXAONE 4.5 (head_size 64 or 128, rows = tokens * heads).

## Fix

- Pass `rows` to the `rms_norm`, `pre_rms_norm`, `fused_ln` and `fused_residual_ln` kernels.
- Derive the row index from the expression already used for `block_offset`, and mask the global loads and stores of rows past the end.
- Threads past the end still take part in the block reductions, so the grid and block shape stay the same. In-bounds outputs are bitwise unchanged.

Same change as #8830 makes for the v1 kernels in `csrc/transformer/inference`.

## Tests

- Every kernel output in `test_rms_norm.py`, `test_post_ln.py`, `test_pre_ln.py` and the new `test_ln.py` (`CUDAFPLN` had no test in-tree) is allocated in front of 256 canary rows. A write past the last row fails under plain pytest, without compute-sanitizer.
- One sub-block shape per threads-per-row dispatch (1, 2, 4, 8, 16), each with one row more than fits in a block, in fp32, fp16 and bf16.
- `assert_rows_independent`: each row of a batched launch must match the same row run alone, within the dtype tolerance. The generic bf16 tolerance (rtol 0.48) is loose enough to accept a row normalized with its neighbour's statistics, so the norm tests use (3e-2, 1e-2) for bf16, measured with a 5x margin over all five kernels and the existing large shapes. No global tolerance change.

## Test results

Hardware: 1x NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121, aarch64), driver 580.126.09, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130, Python 3.13.2.

```
pytest tests/unit/inference/v2/kernels/core_ops/test_rms_norm.py \
       tests/unit/inference/v2/kernels/core_ops/test_post_ln.py \
       tests/unit/inference/v2/kernels/core_ops/test_pre_ln.py \
       tests/unit/inference/v2/kernels/core_ops/test_ln.py -m inference_v2_ops
```

| kernels | passed | failed | skipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| `master` (67ec1961) + this branch's tests | 92 | 108 | 3 |
| this branch | 200 | 0 | 3 |

Measured on 5e2f6ea4. The current revision (3f70aeb7) trims the shape matrix and relaxes the row check to tolerance; the re-run on the same machine is pending and this table will be updated. Every failure on `master` is a sub-block case failing on the canary assertion. The skips are fp32 with 65-128 channels (#8827, see below).

<details>
<summary>compute-sanitizer memcheck (reads as well as writes)</summary>

Each of the four kernels on exactly sized `[rows, channels]` tensors with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck`, 11 shapes covering every threads-per-row dispatch and the in-place path:

| | result |
|---|---|
| `master` kernels | `Invalid __global__ read of size 16 bytes` in `rms_norm` / `fused_ln` / `fused_residual_ln`, 262 errors over the 11 shapes, then a sticky launch failure |
| this branch | `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors` |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Throughput (GB10, median of 200 CUDA-event timings, master -> branch, microseconds)</summary>

| dtype | channels | rows | rms_norm | fused_ln | post_ln | pre_ln |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp16 | 4096 | 1 | 7.62 -> 7.58 | 7.65 -> 7.62 | 7.74 -> 7.71 | 7.84 -> 7.74 |
| fp16 | 4096 | 4096 | 279.9 -> 281.1 | 280.3 -> 281.3 | 419.7 -> 421.6 | 566.7 -> 571.1 |
| fp16 | 8192 | 4096 | 561.7 -> 558.9 | 552.0 -> 552.9 | 843.2 -> 842.6 | 1151 -> 1143 |
| bf16 | 8192 | 4096 | 563.9 -> 558.8 | 553.4 -> 551.9 | 841.4 -> 840.6 | 1144 -> 1136 |
| fp16 | 128 | 2560 (EXAONE4 Q, 64 tokens) | 7.46 -> 7.30 | | | |

All within +-1%, inside round-to-round noise. In-range outputs of all five wrappers were compared bitwise against `master` over 2430 (kernel, dtype, channels, rows) combinations: no differences.

</details>

## Compatibility matrix

- **Validated:** inference v2 core ops on CUDA; fp16 and bf16 for 8-128 channels (sub-block schedule) and the existing 1024-14432 channel shapes; fp32 for 4-64 channels and the large shapes.
- **Not validated:** ROCm builds, pre-sm_80 GPUs, end-to-end inference v2 model runs (e.g. EXAONE4 through the ragged engine).
- **Not applicable:** ZeRO stage, offload, training parallelism. Inference-only kernels.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR references #8831. #8830 (OOB rows), #8743 (`rows == 0`) and #8827 (fp32 65-128 channels launches no kernel) change only the v1 kernels under `csrc/transformer/inference/csrc/`. The v1 kernels, the v2 rms and layer norm kernels, and the other v2 kernels under `kernels/{core_ops,ragged_ops}` were checked; only the v1 and v2 norm kernels pack rows per block this way.

<details>
<summary>Related v2 defects not fixed here (same on master)</summary>

- fp32 with 65-128 channels: `threads_per_group == 32` falls through the sub-block dispatch and no kernel is launched (v2 sibling of #8827). The LN tests skip that cell with an explicit reason.
- `rows == 0` divides by zero in all four v2 launchers (v2 sibling of #8743).
- `rms_norm.cpp` has no `dim() == 2` or contiguity check; `layer_norm.cpp` flattens 3-D inputs, so the two bindings disagree.
- `block_offset` is `int` in all four kernels and overflows past 2^31 elements. The new `row` index adds no overflow of its own.
- `csrc/quantization/quantize.cu` (`cached_quantization`) uses the same row packing with bounded stores but unbounded loads.
- `get_dtypes()` in the v2 test utils caches the first caller's filtered list, so under the directory-level CI invocation later callers lose fp32 (found by the Codex review here). Split out into its own PR so this one stays a kernel fix.

</details>

## AI assistance

This change was written with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above on the hardware listed.

files.patch:
@@ -44,3 +44,42 @@ def allclose(x, y, tolerances: Tuple[int, int] = None):
     else:
         rtol, atol = tolerances
     return torch.allclose(x, y, rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
+
+
+CANARY_VALUE = 1000.0
+
+# The generic bf16 tolerance (rtol 0.48) is loose enough to accept a row normalized with its neighbour's
+# statistics. A row norm's bf16 output is accurate to well under this, so the norm tests use it instead.
+NORM_BF16_TOLERANCES = (3e-2, 1e-2)
+
+
+def norm_tolerances(dtype: torch.dtype):
+    if dtype == torch.bfloat16:
+        return NORM_BF16_TOLERANCES
+    return None
+
+
+def allocate_output_with_canary(rows: int, channels: int, dtype: torch.dtype, canary_rows: int = 256):
+    """Allocate a ``[rows, channels]`` output that is directly followed in memory by ``canary_rows`` rows
+    filled with ``CANARY_VALUE``. A kernel that writes past the last row overwrites the canary, which plain
+    pytest can then detect (the value is finite, so NaN written past the end is detected as well). The default
+    covers the largest sub-block schedule (256 rows per block), so even a full block of overrun stays inside
+    the canary instead of spilling into neighbouring allocations.
+    Returns (output, canary)."""
+    buffer = torch.full((rows + canary_rows, channels),
+                        CANARY_VALUE,
+                        dtype=dtype,
+                        device=get_accelerator().current_device_name())
+    return buffer[:rows], buffer[rows:]
+
+
+def assert_rows_independent(run_rows, batched_outputs: Tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]):
+    """Every row of a batched launch must match the same row run on its own, within the norm tolerance for
+    its dtype. Rows that share a thread block must not see each other's statistics; a per-row reference alone
+    cannot tell that apart from ordinary rounding at bf16 precision. ``run_rows(start, end)`` runs the kernel on
+    input rows ``[start, end)`` and returns its outputs in the same order as ``batched_outputs``."""
+    rows = batched_outputs[0].size(0)
+    for row in range(rows):
+        for single, batched in zip(run_rows(row, row + 1), batched_outputs):
+            assert allclose(single, batched[row:row + 1],
+                            norm_tolerances(single.dtype)), f"row {row} differs when run on its own"

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+# DeepSpeed Team
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from deepspeed.accelerator import get_accelerator
+from deepspeed.inference.v2.kernels.core_ops import CUDAFPLN
+from ....v2.inference_test_utils import (get_dtypes, allclose, allocate_output_with_canary, assert_rows_independent,
+                                         norm_tolerances, CANARY_VALUE)
+
+
+def reference_implementation(hidden_states: torch.Tensor, gamma: torch.Tensor, beta: torch.Tensor,
+                             epsilon: float) -> torch.Tensor:
+    hidden_states_f = hidden_states.to(torch.float32)
+    gamma_f = gamma.to(torch.float32)
+    beta_f = beta.to(torch.float32)
+    return torch.nn.functional.layer_norm(hidden_states_f, (hidden_states_f.size(-1), ),
+                                          weight=gamma_f,
+                                          bias=beta_f,
+                                          eps=epsilon).to(hidden_states.dtype)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.inference_v2_ops
+# The shapes with <= 128 channels pack several rows into one thread block (16 to 256 rows per block, depending
+# on dtype and channels) and have one row more than fits in a block, so the last block is partially filled and
+# must not touch rows past the end. Together they cover every threads-per-row dispatch in fp32 and fp16.
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens, channels", [(1, 4096), (37, 2048), (112, 14432), (1024, 6144), (33, 64), (33, 128),
+                                              (65, 32), (129, 16), (257, 8)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", get_dtypes())
+def test_cuda_ln(tokens: int, channels: int, dtype: torch.dtype) -> None:
+    if dtype == torch.float32 and 64 < channels <= 128:
+        pytest.skip("fp32 with 65-128 channels launches no kernel, see #8827")
+
+    # Input vals
+    hidden_states = torch.randn((tokens, channels), dtype=dtype, device=get_accelerator().current_device_name())
+    gamma = torch.randn((channels), dtype=dtype, device=get_accelerator().current_device_name())
+    beta = torch.rand((channels), dtype=dtype, device=get_accelerator().current_device_name())
+    epsilon = 1e-5
+
+    # Reference output
+    ref_output = reference_implementation(hidden_states, gamma, beta, epsilon)
+
+    # New output

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent the dtype cache from skipping fp32 cases**

Under the full inference-v2 CI invocation in `.github/workflows/nv-a6000.yml:61-63`, collection reaches `test_bias_activation.py:66-68` before this module, and that decorator calls `get_dtypes(include_float=False)`. Since `inference_test_utils.py:25-37` caches the resulting half-only list globally, this check skips both explicit `DtypeEnum.fp32` cases even on fp32-capable hardware; only the targeted three-file command happens to seed the cache with fp32 first. This leaves normal CI without fp32 coverage of the new row bounds, so test optional bf16 support directly (or make the cache respect `include_float`) instead of using the shared cached list here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Pushed bbef33fd after an adversarial review pass (two independent reviewers plus the Codex finding above). Kernel diff is unchanged; the evidence around it was the weak part:

- `get_dtypes()` cache fix so fp32 cases actually run under the directory-level CI invocation (Codex finding; it affected every `get_dtypes()` caller, not just this file).
- `fused_ln` / `CUDAFPLN` had no test anywhere in-tree: added `test_ln.py`.
- Sub-block shapes now cover every threads-per-row dispatch (1-16): 17 / 33 / 65 / 129 rows, 16-128 channels.
- `assert_rows_independent`: each row of a batched launch must be bitwise equal to the row run alone. The bf16 tolerance (rtol 0.48) alone cannot see one row's reduction leaking into a neighbour, so the bf16 cases were effectively canary-only before.
- `test_exaone4.py` exercises the real `_apply_qk_norm` with the real kernels as the inference-level path that motivated the fix.
- Description now lists the v2 siblings that are **not** fixed here (`rows == 0` as in #8743, fp32 65-128 channels as in #8827, and the unbounded loads in `quantize.cu`), narrows the fp32 claim to <= 64 channels, and adds before/after throughput numbers (all within +-1%).

Branch: 157 passed. Same tests on master's kernels: 78 failed / 79 passed.

Pushed 5e2f6ea4 after a second independent review pass. Kernel diff still unchanged.

- Dropped the stub-based `test_exaone4.py`: whether it failed on master depended on where the caching allocator placed K relative to Q (2-3 of 6 layouts per run), and it coupled to private attribute names. The EXAONE4 shape ((tokens * heads, 128) fp16 / bf16) is covered deterministically by the kernel-level canary tests; the description says why no model-level test is included.
- The bf16 oracle was the real gap: at the generic bf16 tolerance a neighbour-row-variance leak passes `allclose` 50/50. Norm tests now use (rtol 3e-2, atol 1e-2), measured 5x margin across all five kernels and 13 shapes; no global tolerance change. `assert_rows_independent` stays, documented as pinning the current schedule property rather than the norm contract.
- The 'every threads-per-row dispatch' claim was false for 1 thread per row: added fp32/4 and fp16/8 at 257 rows, plus (33, 128) in the LN tests (fp32 skipped there with an explicit #8827 reason). Canary depth raised to a full 256-row block.
- 'Not fixed here' now also lists the `rms_norm.cpp` 2-D / contiguity gap and the int32 `block_offset` overflow.

Branch: 200 passed, 3 skipped. Same tests on master's kernels: 108 failed / 92 passed, all on the canary. Note that no CI workflow has run on this PR yet (`action_required`).
